question.en: How Much Is the Medicare Levy?
question.es: ¿Cuánto Es el Impuesto de Medicare (Medicare Levy)?

shortAnswer.en: It depends: 1.45% for employees, 2.9% self-employed, plus 0.9% for high earners.
shortAnswer.es: Depende: 1.45% para empleados, 2.9% autónomo, más 0.9% para ingresos altos.

fullAnswer.en: It depends on how income is earned. Employees pay 1.45% of wages toward Medicare in 2026 and employers match that amount, for a combined 2.9% with no wage cap. Self-employed workers pay the full 2.9% themselves through SECA, and anyone earning more than $200,000 (single) or $250,000 (married filing jointly) in 2026 also owes an extra 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on the income above that threshold.
fullAnswer.es: Depende de cómo se gane el ingreso. Los empleados pagan 1.45% de su salario para Medicare en 2026 y el empleador iguala esa cantidad, para un total combinado de 2.9% sin tope salarial. Los trabajadores autónomos pagan el 2.9% completo ellos mismos a través de SECA, y quienes ganan más de $200,000 (soltero) o $250,000 (casado declarando en conjunto) en 2026 también deben un 0.9% adicional de Impuesto Adicional de Medicare sobre el ingreso que supere ese umbral.

h1.en: How Much Is the Medicare Levy? (2026 Medicare Tax Rates)

introParagraphs.en: The United States does not have a tax officially called the Medicare Levy; that name belongs to Australia's public health system funding mechanism. What most people searching this question actually want to know is how much comes out of a US paycheck for Medicare, and the answer has three moving parts: a flat base rate that everyone pays, an extra surtax that only high earners pay, and a separate structure for the self-employed.
introParagraphs.es: Estados Unidos no tiene un impuesto llamado oficialmente Medicare Levy; ese nombre pertenece al mecanismo de financiamiento del sistema público de salud de Australia. Lo que la mayoría de las personas que buscan esta pregunta realmente quieren saber es cuánto se descuenta de un cheque de pago en EE.UU. para Medicare, y la respuesta tiene tres partes: una tasa base fija que todos pagan, un impuesto adicional que solo pagan los ingresos altos, y una estructura separada para los trabajadores autónomos.

introParagraphs.en: The 2026 Medicare tax rate for employees, the Additional Medicare Tax for high earners, how self-employment tax (SECA) works, and how this payroll tax differs from the Medicare Part B premium you pay after enrolling are all covered below. For enrollment and coverage questions, see [Medicare eligibility](/glossary/medicare-savings-program) or check [what Medicare actually costs](/glossary/most-medicare-can-cost).
introParagraphs.es: Esta guía detalla la tasa de impuesto de Medicare 2026 para empleados, el Impuesto Adicional de Medicare para ingresos altos, cómo funciona el impuesto de autoempleo (SECA), y cómo este impuesto de nómina difiere de la prima de la Parte B de Medicare que paga después de inscribirse.

heading.en: The Standard Medicare Tax Rate in 2026
heading.es: La Tasa Estándar del Impuesto de Medicare en 2026

paragraphs.en: Every paycheck in the United States carries a Medicare tax line separate from federal income tax withholding. In 2026, employees pay 1.45% of every dollar of wages toward Medicare, and employers match that amount dollar for dollar, for a combined 2.9%. Unlike the Social Security payroll tax, which stops once wages hit the 2026 taxable maximum of $184,500, the Medicare tax has no wage cap; it has applied to every dollar of covered earnings since Congress removed the cap in 1994. This flat 2.9% combined rate flows directly into the Medicare Part A Hospital Insurance (HI) Trust Fund, the account that pays hospital, skilled nursing, and hospice claims for Original Medicare beneficiaries.

heading.en: The Additional Medicare Tax for High Earners (2026)
heading.es: El Impuesto Adicional de Medicare para Ingresos Altos (2026)

paragraphs.en: The Affordable Care Act added a second layer on top of the standard 2.9% rate starting in 2013: the Additional Medicare Tax. In 2026, this extra 0.9% applies to wages and self-employment income above $200,000 for single filers, $250,000 for married couples filing jointly, and $125,000 for married filing separately. Employers must start withholding the 0.9% surtax automatically once an employee's wages exceed $200,000 in a calendar year, regardless of the employee's actual filing status or a spouse's income; workers reconcile the correct amount on IRS Form 8959 when they file. These thresholds have never been adjusted for inflation since 2013, so more workers cross them every year as wages rise. Revenue from the Additional Medicare Tax, unlike the employer-matched base rate, comes entirely from the employee and flows into the same Part A Hospital Insurance Trust Fund.

heading.es: Autoempleo y el Impuesto de Medicare (SECA)

paragraphs.en: Self-employed workers pay Medicare tax through the Self-Employment Contributions Act (SECA) instead of FICA, but the underlying math is nearly identical. The 2026 SECA rate is 15.3% of net self-employment earnings, made up of 12.4% for Social Security, capped at the $184,500 taxable maximum, and 2.9% for Medicare, which has no cap. Because self-employed people do not have a separate employer to split the cost, they effectively pay both the employee and employer shares of the Medicare tax themselves. The Additional Medicare Tax also applies to self-employment income above the same $200,000, $250,000, or $125,000 thresholds used for wages, and the two income types are combined when checking whether a filer has crossed the threshold. Self-employed taxpayers can deduct half of the SECA tax as an above-the-line adjustment to income on Form 1040 Schedule 1.

heading.en: How the Medicare Tax Differs from Medicare Premiums
heading.es: En Qué Se Diferencia el Impuesto de Medicare de las Primas de Medicare

paragraphs.en: The Medicare tax withheld from a paycheck is not the same thing as a Medicare premium, and mixing the two up is the most common source of confusion. The payroll tax funds Medicare Part A, so most beneficiaries who worked at least 40 quarters (10 years) pay no separate premium for hospital coverage under Original Medicare. Medicare Part B, by contrast, is funded mostly through general tax revenue plus a monthly premium that beneficiaries pay directly: $202.90 per month at the standard rate in 2026. Medicare Part D prescription drug plans, Medicare Advantage plans, and Medigap supplemental policies all charge their own separate premiums set by private insurers, none of which come from the payroll tax at all. In short, the Medicare tax pays into Part A while nearly every other piece of Medicare coverage is funded through premiums and general revenue, not the payroll tax.

heading.en: Who Is Exempt from the Medicare Tax
heading.es: Quién Está Exento del Impuesto de Medicare

paragraphs.en: A small number of workers are legally exempt from paying the Medicare tax. Members of certain recognized religious sects that are conscientiously opposed to accepting public insurance benefits can file IRS Form 4029 to opt out of both Social Security and Medicare taxes. Nonresident alien students, scholars, and researchers on F-1, J-1, M-1, or Q-1 visas are generally exempt from Medicare tax on wages earned performing the services allowed under their visa, typically for their first five calendar years of US presence. Some state and local government employees hired before 1986 who are covered by an alternative public retirement system remain outside the Medicare tax system, and workers from countries with a Social Security totalization agreement with the United States may be exempt while temporarily assigned here by a foreign employer.

heading.en: Is the 'Medicare Levy' in Australia the Same Thing?
heading.es: ¿El 'Medicare Levy' de Australia Es lo Mismo?

paragraphs.en: Searchers sometimes land on this question because 'Medicare levy' is the official name of a different program entirely. Australia funds its public health system, also called Medicare, with a Medicare levy equal to 2% of taxable income, collected through its tax office rather than a payroll withholding split between employer and employee. Australia also has a separate Medicare Levy Surcharge for higher earners who do not carry private hospital insurance. The United States has no tax officially called a 'Medicare levy'; the closest US equivalent is the payroll-based Medicare tax described above, plus the Additional Medicare Tax for high earners. The two programs share a name but operate under completely different rules, rates, and government agencies.

heading.en: Do 401(k) or HSA Contributions Change What You Owe?
heading.es: ¿Las Contribuciones a 401(k) o HSA Cambian lo que Debe?

paragraphs.en: Pre-tax 401(k) contributions reduce the wages reported for federal income tax, but they do not reduce Medicare wages. Box 5 of Form W-2, which reports Medicare wages, still includes 401(k) deferrals, so contributing to a 401(k) does not lower your Medicare tax bill. Health savings account (HSA) contributions made through an employer's Section 125 cafeteria plan work differently: those dollars are excluded from Box 5 as well as Box 1, which means payroll HSA contributions genuinely reduce the wages subject to the 1.45% Medicare tax. HSA contributions made directly by an individual outside of payroll, rather than through payroll deduction, do not get this Medicare tax break.

heading.en: Next Steps: How to Check and Reconcile Your Medicare Tax
heading.es: Próximos Pasos: Cómo Verificar y Conciliar Su Impuesto de Medicare

paragraphs.en: Confirming how much Medicare tax was actually withheld takes only a few minutes with documents most workers already have on hand each year.

list.en: Check Box 5 (Medicare wages and tips) and Box 6 (Medicare tax withheld) on your W-2; Box 6 should equal 1.45% of Box 5 unless the Additional Medicare Tax applied.
list.es: Verifique la Casilla 5 (salarios de Medicare) y la Casilla 6 (impuesto de Medicare retenido) en su W-2; la Casilla 6 debe ser igual al 1.45% de la Casilla 5 salvo que aplique el Impuesto Adicional de Medicare.

list.en: Self-employed filers calculate the 2.9% Medicare portion on Schedule SE when filing the 2026 Form 1040.
list.es: Los declarantes autónomos calculan la parte de 2.9% de Medicare en el Anexo SE al presentar el Formulario 1040 de 2026.

list.en: Anyone whose wages, self-employment income, or combined income crossed $200,000 (single), $250,000 (married filing jointly), or $125,000 (married filing separately) in 2026 reconciles the Additional Medicare Tax on IRS Form 8959.
list.es: Cualquier persona cuyo salario, ingreso por autoempleo o ingreso combinado superó $200,000 (soltero), $250,000 (casado en conjunto) o $125,000 (casado por separado) en 2026 concilia el Impuesto Adicional de Medicare en el Formulario 8959 del IRS.

list.en: Workers with multiple employers who each withheld only up to their own $200,000 threshold may still owe additional tax at filing even though no single employer over-withheld; Form 8959 catches this gap.
list.es: Los trabajadores con varios empleadores que cada uno retuvo solo hasta su propio umbral de $200,000 pueden aún deber impuesto adicional al presentar la declaración; el Formulario 8959 detecta esta brecha.

list.en: Questions about a specific paycheck or W-2 amount should go to a tax professional or irs.gov/taxtopics/tc560; questions about Medicare Part A or Part B enrollment go to medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE.
list.es: Las preguntas sobre un cheque de pago o W-2 específico deben dirigirse a un profesional de impuestos o irs.gov; las preguntas sobre inscripción en la Parte A o Parte B de Medicare van a medicare.gov o 1-800-MEDICARE.

en.question: What is the Medicare tax rate for 2026?
en.answer: The base Medicare tax rate in 2026 is 1.45% of wages paid by the employee and 1.45% matched by the employer, for a combined 2.9%. There is no wage cap, so this rate applies to every dollar earned. Self-employed workers pay the full 2.9% themselves through SECA. High earners also owe an Additional Medicare Tax of 0.9% above set income thresholds.

en.question: What is the Additional Medicare Tax and who has to pay it?
en.answer: The Additional Medicare Tax is an extra 0.9% created by the Affordable Care Act in 2013. In 2026, it applies to wages and self-employment income above $200,000 for single filers, $250,000 for married filing jointly, and $125,000 for married filing separately. Only the employee pays it, with no employer match, and the thresholds have never been adjusted for inflation.

en.question: Does the Medicare tax have a wage cap like Social Security?
en.answer: No. The Medicare tax has applied to every dollar of covered wages since Congress removed its wage cap in 1994. Social Security tax, by contrast, stops once earnings hit the 2026 taxable maximum of $184,500. This is why high earners see Social Security withholding disappear from their paychecks late in the year while Medicare withholding continues.

en.question: How much Medicare tax do self-employed workers pay?
en.answer: Self-employed workers pay 2.9% of net self-employment earnings toward Medicare through SECA, since they cover both the employee and employer shares themselves. This is part of the broader 15.3% SECA rate that also includes 12.4% for Social Security, capped at $184,500 in 2026. Half of the total SECA tax is deductible on Form 1040 Schedule 1.

en.question: Is the Medicare tax the same as my Medicare Part B premium?
en.answer: No. The Medicare tax is a payroll tax that funds Medicare Part A, so most people pay no separate Part A premium after 40 quarters of work. Medicare Part B is funded differently, mostly by general tax revenue plus a monthly premium of $202.90 at the standard 2026 rate, which beneficiaries pay directly and separately from any payroll tax.

en.question: Who is exempt from paying the Medicare tax?
en.answer: A limited group is exempt: members of certain religious sects who file IRS Form 4029, nonresident alien students and scholars on F-1, J-1, M-1, or Q-1 visas (typically the first 5 years), some state and local government employees hired before 1986, and workers covered under a Social Security totalization agreement while temporarily working in the US for a foreign employer.

en.question: Is Australia's Medicare levy the same as the US Medicare tax?
en.answer: No. Australia's Medicare levy is a 2% tax on taxable income that funds Australia's public health system and is collected through its national tax office. The United States has no tax officially named a 'Medicare levy'; the closest equivalent is the US payroll-based Medicare tax (1.45% to 2.9%) plus the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax for high earners.

en.question: Do 401(k) or HSA contributions lower how much Medicare tax I pay?
en.answer: 401(k) contributions do not reduce Medicare tax; they still count as Medicare wages on Box 5 of your W-2. HSA contributions made through an employer's Section 125 payroll deduction are excluded from Medicare wages, so those specific payroll HSA contributions do genuinely lower the 1.45% Medicare tax owed on that portion of income.

es.question: ¿Cuál es la tasa del impuesto de Medicare para 2026?
es.answer: La tasa base del impuesto de Medicare en 2026 es 1.45% del salario pagado por el empleado y 1.45% igualado por el empleador, para un total combinado de 2.9%. No hay tope salarial, así que esta tasa aplica a cada dólar ganado. Los trabajadores autónomos pagan el 2.9% completo ellos mismos a través de SECA.

es.question: ¿Qué es el Impuesto Adicional de Medicare y quién debe pagarlo?
es.answer: El Impuesto Adicional de Medicare es un 0.9% extra creado por la Ley de Cuidado de Salud Asequible (ACA) en 2013. En 2026, aplica a salarios e ingresos por autoempleo por encima de $200,000 para solteros, $250,000 para casados que declaran en conjunto, y $125,000 para casados que declaran por separado.

es.question: ¿El impuesto de Medicare tiene un tope salarial como el Seguro Social?
es.answer: No. El impuesto de Medicare se aplica a cada dólar de salario cubierto desde que el Congreso eliminó su tope salarial en 1994. El impuesto de Seguro Social, en cambio, se detiene al llegar al máximo tributable de $184,500 en 2026.

es.question: ¿Cuánto impuesto de Medicare pagan los trabajadores autónomos?
es.answer: Los trabajadores autónomos pagan 2.9% de sus ganancias netas por autoempleo hacia Medicare a través de SECA, ya que cubren ambas partes, empleado y empleador. Esto es parte de la tasa SECA más amplia de 15.3% que también incluye 12.4% para el Seguro Social, con tope de $184,500 en 2026.

es.question: ¿El impuesto de Medicare es lo mismo que mi prima de la Parte B de Medicare?
es.answer: No. El impuesto de Medicare es un impuesto de nómina que financia la Parte A de Medicare, por lo que la mayoría de las personas no pagan una prima separada de la Parte A después de 40 trimestres de trabajo. La Parte B de Medicare se financia de forma diferente, principalmente con ingresos fiscales generales más una prima mensual de $202.90 a la tasa estándar de 2026.

es.question: ¿Quién está exento de pagar el impuesto de Medicare?
es.answer: Un grupo limitado está exento: miembros de ciertas sectas religiosas que presentan el Formulario 4029 del IRS, estudiantes y académicos extranjeros no residentes con visas F-1, J-1, M-1 o Q-1 (típicamente los primeros 5 años), algunos empleados estatales y locales contratados antes de 1986, y trabajadores cubiertos bajo un acuerdo de totalización del Seguro Social.

es.question: ¿El Medicare Levy de Australia es lo mismo que el impuesto de Medicare de EE.UU.?
es.answer: No. El Medicare levy de Australia es un impuesto del 2% sobre el ingreso tributable que financia el sistema público de salud de Australia. Estados Unidos no tiene un impuesto llamado oficialmente 'Medicare levy'; lo más parecido es el impuesto de Medicare basado en nómina (1.45% a 2.9%) más el 0.9% adicional para ingresos altos.

es.question: ¿Las contribuciones a 401(k) o HSA reducen cuánto impuesto de Medicare pago?
es.answer: Las contribuciones a 401(k) no reducen el impuesto de Medicare; siguen contando como salario de Medicare en la Casilla 5 de su W-2. Las contribuciones a HSA hechas a través de la deducción de nómina del plan Sección 125 del empleador sí se excluyen del salario de Medicare, reduciendo genuinamente el impuesto del 1.45% sobre esa parte del ingreso.
